Definition: a glow (of wind or anger); also a famine (as consuming)
BiblicalUsage: zalʻâphâh means a glow (of wind or anger). In Psalms 11:6 we read, "Upon the wicked he shall rain snares, fire and brimstone, and an horrible tempest..." It appears again in Psalms 119:53: "Horror hath taken hold upon me because of the wicked that forsake thy law."
TheologicalSignificance: zal'aphah is a glow (of wind or anger), and I believe no word in Scripture is wasted, so this one earns its place.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
